grep: Searches for specific patterns or text strings within files and outputs matching lines.
cd: Changes the current working directory in the command-line interface.
wget: A non-interactive network downloader used to retrieve files from the web via HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP.
curl: A command-line tool for transferring data to or from a server using various protocols like HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, etc.
nat: Network Address Translation maps IP addresses in a packet header while in transit across a routing device.
ls: Lists directory contents, showing files and folders inside the current working directory.
pwd: Prints the absolute path of the current working directory.
mkdir: Creates a new directory or folder at the specified location.
chmod: Changes file or directory access permissions in Unix-like operating systems.
chown: Changes the user and group ownership of file system files and directories.
ssh: Secure Shell protocol for secure remote login and other secure network services over an insecure network.
iptables: A user-space application program that allows a system administrator to configure the IP packet filter rules of the Linux kernel firewall.
systemctl: A command-line tool to inspect and manage the systemd system and service manager.
ping: Tests the reachability of a host across an Internet Protocol network and measures round-trip time.
ipconfig: A Windows utility used to display all current TCP/IP network configuration values and refresh DHCP and DNS settings.
powershell: A task automation and configuration management framework from Microsoft, consisting of a powerful shell and scripting language.
cmd: The command-line interpreter application on Windows operating systems.
registry: A hierarchical database that stores low-level settings for the Microsoft Windows operating system and for applications.
active-directory: A Microsoft directory service that manages permissions and access to network resources in a Windows Domain environment.
snat: Source Network Address Translation modifies the source IP address in the IP header of outbound packets, commonly used for sharing a single public IP.
dnat: Destination Network Address Translation modifies the destination IP address of incoming packets, often used for port forwarding.
pat: Port Address Translation (or NAT overload) maps multiple private IP addresses to a single public IP address using different ports.
subnet: A logical subdivision of an IP network, allowing a network to be partitioned into smaller, manageable segments.
vlan: Virtual Local Area Network partitions a physical network into multiple logical networks for security and traffic management.
dhcp: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automatically assigns IP addresses and network configuration parameters to devices on a network.
dns: Domain Name System translates human-friendly domain names into machine-readable IP addresses.
firewall: A network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules.
ldap: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol used for accessing and maintaining distributed directory information services over an IP network.
raid: Redundant Array of Independent Disks data storage virtualization technology that combines multiple physical disk drive components into one or more logical units for redundancy or performance.
hypervisor: Software, firmware, or hardware that creates and runs virtual machines (e.g., VMware, Hyper-V, KVM).
ansible: An open-source software provisioning, configuration management, and application-deployment tool using infrastructure as code.
kubernetes: An open-source container orchestration system for automating software deployment, scaling, and management.
